courseTitle: NativeScript + Angular: Build Native iOS, Android & Web Apps

cues.en: Now that we worked on the styling off the app and it doesn't look too shabby, let's work on fetching
the user input and handling it correctly.
And that mostly means working on the forms, also showing validation errors and storing that input somewhere.
That is exactly what we'll have a look at in this module.
Now, it's important to understand that we'll use angle form features here since we use native script
with Angular and there it's important to keep in mind that Angular has two approaches when it comes
to handling forms, the template derivative forms approach and the reactive forms approach.
Now, if that tells you nothing, definitely, as always, dive into some dedicated angler resources
to learn more about these approaches.
The general idea is that in the template driven forward approach, you use the engie model directive
mostly to set up controls and listen to their input in the reactive forms approach.
You configure your foreman to type code and then just tell ANGULAR which input in your template belongs
to which object, so to say, in your typescript code.
Now, native script fully supports the reactive forms approach and partially supports the template driven
forms approach.
Partial because there is no foreign element in native script.
And therefore this inferred forms object, which you have in Angola for WEAP does not really exist in
that form in native script or is a little bit harder to work with in native script, to be precise.
Now, we can absolutely use to we're binding, though, we can use the energy model directive and we
can get access to all the user input and I will show you how this works in this module as well as I
will dive into the reactive forms approach.
Well, then I'll have a look at how we can validate user input, show an error message and all of that.
